_description: Pillar 8 — Plans-tree governance (per-pillar rule model). Carries the plans-pillar _rules[] SoT (home=plans; R-29/R-30/R-31/R-56 skill-tier + R-61/R-62/R-63 master/sub reconciler-tier), the canonical 6-state plan lifecycle, the subplan_rules.metadata_flow orchestrator-worker contract, the per-plan ADR ledger convention, and the structural config the plans-tree is validated against. Loaded by hooks/pre-write-guard.sh + the librarian plan/backlog capabilities.

_design_notes.consumer: hooks/pre-write-guard.sh (R-27/R-28 via naming pillar; librarian-only root-file writes), skills/librarian/capabilities/{plan-index,backlog-index}.sh, the librarian reconciler (R-61/R-62/R-63 cross-file)
_design_notes.evolution_protocol: R-37 documentary lockstep — there is NO write-time DENY for R-37; enforcement = git commit-boundary atomicity + librarian governance-parity-audit at session-close. This pillar + its schema + contracts + hook move in one commit.

_rules.rule_text: Backlog row size is bounded — a row in the unified _backlog.md carries only a current-state pointer; session history lives in the satellite, not the row. backlog-hygiene flags over-long rows.
_rules.failure_mode: Unbounded backlog rows accrete session narrative inline; the index becomes a log; scan-readability collapses. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.

_rules.rule_text: Backlog sentinel pattern — the row carries the current-state pointer; the satellite at the plan dir / handoff.md is the single source of session history. backlog-hygiene validates the pattern.
_rules.failure_mode: Drift between row and satellite; history scattered. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.

_rules.rule_text: Backlog sentinel pattern (companion to R-30) — sentinel-bounded row regions are librarian-regenerated; operator narrative is preserved outside the sentinels. backlog-hygiene validates parity.
_rules.failure_mode: Hand-edits inside sentinel regions are clobbered on regen, or stale regions diverge. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.

_rules.rule_text: Every backlog row (idea note or {researching,planned} manifest) carries a disposition signal (FIX NOW / ABSORB / STANDALONE / DEFERRED). backlog-hygiene escalates severity Warning -> Alert by stale_for_days against backlog_row.stale_advisory_days when a disposition is missing.
_rules.failure_mode: Undisposed backlog rows float indefinitely; the GTD review loop has nothing to act on. Skill-enforced (backlog-hygiene), never write-time.

_rules.rule_text: Master sub_plans[] aggregation-integrity: the master manifest's sub_plans[].status read-replica MUST agree with each sub-plan's real published status. Cross-file invariant enforced by the librarian reconciler (NOT write-time) — extends trinity-drift-detect.sh / drift-sweep.sh with the master<->sub aggregation axis; detects (and optionally --fix) drift.
_rules.failure_mode: A master's sub_plans[] read-replica goes stale against the subs' real status; the master shows a sub as in-progress that has actually completed (or vice-versa); orchestration decisions read a phantom aggregate. Cross-file -> reconciler at session-close, never a blocking write-time path.

_rules.rule_text: Sub-publishes-upward: a sub-plan publishes its status + graduation_timestamp upward to the master (the master reads them into sub_plans[]); a sub MUST NOT mutate the master aggregate directly. Cross-file invariant enforced by the librarian reconciler (NOT write-time).
_rules.failure_mode: A sub-plan fails to publish a status transition, or attempts to write the master aggregate directly, breaking the pull-based read-replica model. Cross-file -> reconciler at session-close.

_rules.rule_text: Sub-peer-isolation: a sub-plan manifest MUST NOT carry a dependencies edge to a sibling sub-plan — route through the master manifest (the orchestrator-worker invariant: workers report only to the orchestrator, never to each other). Surfaced as a librarian reconciler drift finding (advisory).
_rules.failure_mode: A sub declares a direct dependency on a sibling sub, recreating the agent-teams peer model the orchestrator-worker model deliberately rejects (MAST coordination-failure class). Advisory drift finding at session-close.

enforcement_layer: pre-write-guard.sh plan-artifact frontmatter gate (write-time DENY on the 4 canonical basenames; marker R65_PROMOTED)
schemas/plans-schema.json (the filename-to-type map + per-type required[] cohort the gate reads)
_rules.failure_mode: A canonical plan artifact (spec.md / tasks.md / handoff.md / 00-ideation-brief.md) written with a missing or non-canonical type: field is invisible or mis-routed to every type-keyed consumer (renderers, validators, index walkers). Promoted from advisory to write-time DENY once the corpus floor measured clean (3 named historical stragglers corpus-wide at promotion).
_rules.rule_text: The 4 canonical Markdown plan artifacts must carry the canonical type: for their basename (spec.md -> spec, tasks.md -> tasks, handoff.md -> handoff, 00-ideation-brief.md -> ideation-brief) per schemas/plans-schema.json. Missing or mismatched type: DENIES the write; the deny message carries the canonical frontmatter stub (DERIVE: no status: in artifact frontmatter). Escape hatch for field over-fire: R65_ALLOW_OVERRIDE=1 downgrades the gate to the legacy advisory for that write. All other arms of the plan-frontmatter block (status-line enum, library/binder reach) remain advisory.
_rules.legacy_label_note: The guard block's emitted advisory strings historically carry the '[R-40 PLAN FRONTMATTER]' (and sibling [R-40 LIBRARY/BINDER]) prefixes and are kept byte-stable for fixture/sentinel continuity — but the bare R-40 id is owned by the frontmatter pillar's provides-canonicality rule. This entry (R-65) is the registered id of the promoted type gate; deny messages name the mechanism and R-65, never the legacy label.
_rules.rollback: R65_ALLOW_OVERRIDE=1 (env, per-write) downgrades to the legacy advisory; a durable rollback is a substance change to this entry's tier + the guard emission branch, one commit, master rebuild + manifest regen coupled.

root_namespace._description: CLOSED plans-root namespace. The plans-tree root admits ONLY the entry classes enumerated in allowed_entry_classes — nothing else. This is the single source of truth read by the write-time root-allowlist guard (hooks/pre-write-guard.sh, positioned before R-27), the sweep-side rule (skills/librarian/capabilities/placement-validate.sh), and the shared classifier hooks/lib/plan-path.sh::classify_root_entry. A root entry matching no allowed class is non-conforming: ask->deny at write-time (advisory-to-blocking rollout), flagged by the sweep. Rationale: session outputs with no owning plan otherwise invent root surfaces whose records get no lifecycle; a closed namespace routes durable artifacts to their owning context instead.

plan_dirs._description: NN-<slug> plan directories (conforming-active; R-27-governed prefix + status).

legacy_flat_plans._description: Depth-1 flat NN-<slug>.md plans — kept in place, not retroactively invalidated (each carries inbound citations). CLOSED class: the scaffolder mints directories only, so no new flat-plan members can appear through the sanctioned path.

root_files._description: Librarian-generated root registry files (also enumerated under root_files above).

funnel_registry_surfaces._description: Enumerated funnel + registry directories: _inbox (pre-plan idea capture), _projects (per-spoke binder registry), _library (universal-only cross-project library). Historical registry documents are deliberately NOT enumerated surfaces — the governance JSON pillar is the live rule source of truth, and a historical map file is not a durable root registry.

dot_entries._description: Leading-dot entries (.git, .gitignore, .DS_Store, .active-plan, dotfiles) are class-exempt so the closed namespace does not fight VCS/OS/pointer machinery.

metadata_flow._description: Orchestrator-worker contract for first-class master/sub-plan structure. Maps onto Claude Code's subagent orchestrator-worker invariant: workers run in isolated contexts, report only to the orchestrator, and NEVER communicate with each other — the deliberate OPPOSITE of the agent-teams peer model. Master/sub aggregation is pull-based and DERIVED: the master sub_plans[] is a librarian-generated read-replica (same trust class as _index.md), NEVER hand-edited.
metadata_flow.aggregation_model: pull-based-derived-read-replica (librarian reconciler reads each sub's published status into the master's sub_plans[]; never hand-edited; same class as _index.md)

required_artifacts._description: Per-transition required artifacts a status flip MUST present. Consumed by the librarian reconciler.

parent_plan_exempt_files: Plan-root files at depth 2 (spec.md, tasks.md, handoff.md, 00-ideation-brief.md, README.md, manifest.json) — they ARE the parent
handoff.md at any depth (append-only session record)

decision_records._description: Per-plan ADR (Architecture Decision Record) ledger. Short, immutable, individually-addressable, supersession-tracked decision records. Optional: a plan with no recorded decisions has no decisions/ dir. Body-structure contract at governance/file-type-contracts/adr.md.json; manifest pointer array at schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: decision_records[].
decision_records.placement_rule: repo-tier (docs/decisions/, 4-digit) IFF the decision changes adopter-inherited foundation behavior; else plan-tier (<plan>/decisions/ADR-NN-<slug>.md, 2-digit).
decision_records.agent_reload_contract: On plan resume, load non-superseded ADRs via manifest.decision_records[] as the decision context — NOT spec-prose archaeology.
decision_records.tooling: NONE (no adr-tools / log4brains). Markdown-in-git + librarian enumeration covers it; bundling violates minimum-viable.
decision_records.immutability: An accepted ADR is immutable. A decision change creates a NEW ADR that supersedes the prior one (prior Status -> superseded-by-ADR-NN); never an in-place edit. Distinct from the spec.md append-amendment pattern.

settled_section._note: Derived settled ledger rendered below the active table by librarian:backlog-index — THREE sources: graduated items joined from plan manifests' promoted_from, absorption joins from plan manifests' absorbed_notes[] (one row per listed note, landing plan named; a note-side row for the same note takes precedence), and inbox notes carrying a terminal resolution (flat or in the settled home); never hand-kept.

backlog_row._stale_advisory_days_note: [advisory_threshold, escalation_threshold] in days for a backlog row missing a disposition. backlog-index emits backlog-row-missing-disposition once per run; backlog-hygiene escalates severity Warning->Alert by stale_for_days against these thresholds (R-56).

inbox._description: Pre-plan idea capture surface. Lightweight per-idea notes at ~/.claude-plans/_inbox/<slug>.md — cheap capture, extended-form body that grows in place, hook-unblocked (hooks/lib/plan-path.sh::classify_plan_path returns is_plan=0 so R-27 prefix/status never fires). Rendered into the unified _backlog.md by librarian:backlog-index. Graduates to a full plan via the idea->plan promote path (migrates body -> 00-ideation-brief.md, scaffolds the NN- quartet, tombstones the note).
inbox._slug_pattern_note: Inbox notes have NO NN- numeric prefix (distinct from plan slugs). The prefix is assigned at graduation, not at capture — avoids prefix burn on discarded ideas.
inbox.body: free-form extended idea content (description / rationale / notes); grows in place across funnel stages until graduation

_status_model_note: Two object types, two vocabularies. (1) Plan manifests carry the ONE canonical 6-state `status` (lifecycle.status_enum below; on plan-manifest-schema.json :: status). (2) Inbox idea notes carry inbox.funnel_status_enum {new, triaged, briefed} — a DIFFERENT object type (a pre-plan idea note, not a plan manifest), NOT collapsed into the 6-state plan status. The inbox funnel is separate from the plan-status enum. backlog_row.status_enum is the documented union shown in the rendered _backlog.md view.

lifecycle._description: ONE canonical 6-state plan `status`. The single authoritative `status` lives on schemas/plan-manifest-schema.json :: status; this block declares the transition gates the librarian reconciler enforces. completed is the sole terminal done-state; archival is a display-only view filter over completed plans, never a status.

in-progress->completed._note: completed = the human's claim that work is done; the sole terminal done-state
